answer: Each epoch opens with a violet beacon pulse no one can predict, and every identity must anchor one fresh proof to it: a short solution to a task seeded by that pulse, bound to its own key so a copy is exposed at once. Two randomly drawn peers re-derive the same proof from the pulse and the key before it counts. An honest agent anchors one proof per epoch. An attacker with a thousand fakes cannot precompute anything before the pulse, and must solve a thousand fresh beacon-seeded tasks every epoch, so the flood's cost rises linearly with every fake and stays unprofitable.
